title: Behavioral Effects & Interference
description: Run experiments where users don't behave like independent units: novelty effects that fade, network effects that contaminate control, and switchback designs that need careful temporal-autocorrelation handling.
focus_concepts: TYPE I AND TYPE II ERRORS
outcomes: You'll distinguish novelty from genuine treatment effects, recognise when network spillover contaminates A/B control, design switchback experiments that account for temporal autocorrelation, and reason about when short-duration tests miss two-sided marketplace steady-state effects.
